# Node graph templates

Templates create a fresh node graph and modifier. Their controls appear as interface inputs in the modifier panel, and every graph contains an explanatory frame. Applying a template never shares its graph with another modifier.

| Template | Category | Scene kinds | Description | What to adjust |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Radial reveal | Animation | splat, mesh, points | Reveal geometry from an adjustable centre as sequencer time advances. | Centre sets the origin, Radius the starting extent, and Speed the expansion per second; scrub the sequencer to preview. |
| Camera coverage cleanup | Clean-up | splat, mesh, points | Remove geometry supported by fewer than a chosen number of capture cameras. | Load dataset cameras, then lower Minimum Views if too much useful geometry disappears. |
| Remove background haze | Clean-up | splat | Remove faint oversized splats that create a milky background. | Raise Max Opacity or lower Min Size to remove more; inspect the result before applying. |
| Remove floater clumps | Clean-up | splat | Remove small disconnected islands while retaining larger surfaces. | Increase Radius to connect nearby splats; increase Min Size to reject larger islands. |
| Remove floaters | Clean-up | splat | Remove low-opacity or isolated splats across the capture. | Tune Min Opacity first, then Isolation Radius and Min Neighbours for detached specks. |
| Scale clamp | Clean-up | splat | Shorten needle-shaped splats without thickening flat surface splats. | Lower Max Aspect to shorten more needle-shaped splats. |
| Autumn grass | Colour | splat | Select green colours in HSV and shift them towards warm autumn tones. | Tune Hue and Hue Range until only foliage or grass is selected, then adjust Hue Shift. |
| Colour grade | Colour | splat | Add contrast, saturation and warmth to the whole capture. | Start with Exposure, Contrast and Saturation; use Temperature for a warmer or cooler result. |
| Colour pop | Colour | splat | Keep one colour range vivid while desaturating everything else. | Set Key Colour to the subject, then adjust Tolerance and Softness for a clean transition. |
| Height fog | Colour | splat, mesh, points | Blend low geometry towards a pale fog colour using a directional height field. | Set Origin near ground level, Up to the scene up axis, and Fog Top above the desired layer. |
| Noise colour variation | Colour | splat, mesh, points | Add scene-scale mottled colour variation driven by procedural noise. | Adjust Scale for patch size, Seed for a new pattern, and Strength for the blend. |
| Posterize | Colour | splat, mesh, points | Reduce colour values to a small number of graphic bands. | Use Levels to choose between a bold graphic effect and a subtler stepped grade. |
| Sharpen subject | Geometry | splat | Sharpen a feathered ellipsoid region while preserving visual coverage. | Move Centre and size Radii around the subject, then adjust Amount and Falloff. |
| Soft edge fade | Geometry | splat | Fade geometry opacity towards the edge of an adjustable subject region. | Set Centre and Radii around the useful capture; Falloff controls the soft edge width. |
| Web export prep | Geometry | splat | Reduce spherical-harmonic detail and decimate for a lightweight web asset. | Set Keep Fraction for the size target; Degree 0 gives the largest reduction. |
| Box crop | Selection | splat, mesh, points | Keep geometry inside an adjustable oriented box. | Set Centre and Size to the desired bounds; use Rotation for non-axis-aligned scenes. |
| Crop showcase | Selection | splat, mesh, points | Keep geometry inside an adjustable ellipsoid for an object-centred presentation. | Position Centre on the subject and expand Radii until the intended object is complete. |

Open **Add Modifier → From template…** or use the suggestions in the Node Editor empty state. User templates are stored under the LichtFeld user configuration directory and respect `LFS_HOME`.

## Save and exchange templates

Use **Save as template…** in a modifier's menu. **My templates** supports Rename and Delete; Import and Export exchange JSON files including the graph interface, frames, notes and referenced groups. User text stays literal; built-in descriptions follow the application language.

## Automation

In the running application, `lf.nodes.templates()` lists metadata and `lf.nodes.apply_template(target, id)` creates a modifier with a fresh graph. `save_template(tree, name, description, category)` and `import_template(path)` return a user-template ID. Use `rename_template(id, name)`, `delete_template(id)` and `export_template(id, path)` to manage it.

MCP exposes the equivalent `nodes.template_list`, `nodes.template_apply`, `nodes.template_save`, `nodes.template_rename`, `nodes.template_delete`, `nodes.template_import` and `nodes.template_export` tools.

## Preview a node

Click the eye in a node header, Ctrl+Shift-click a node, or select it and press **P**. Geometry outputs replace the host's evaluated display temporarily. Field outputs colour the consumer's input geometry; scalar fields show an automatic range in the viewport pill. Press **Esc** or toggle again to return to the stack result. Changing host or removing the previewed node also exits preview. Preview does not alter stored geometry or undo history.

Python: `lf.nodes.preview(target, node, socket=None)` and `lf.nodes.clear_preview()`. MCP: `nodes.preview_set` and `nodes.preview_clear`; `lichtfeld://nodes/editor` includes preview state. Qualify ambiguous names as `<modifier UUID>/<node>` and nested nodes as `<modifier UUID>/<group>/<node>`.
